checks.title: The deployment completes
checks.what_to_do: Follow the recommended route end to end on your own hosting account, from the template or configuration named on the record, and wait for the service to reach a running state.
checks.passing_criteria: The service starts and stays up long enough to be used. A deployment that needs an undocumented manual fix has not passed until that fix is written into the guide.

checks.title: Initial configuration completes
checks.what_to_do: Complete first-run setup: create the first account or credential, apply any database migration, and set the environment values the product needs to be usable.
checks.passing_criteria: The product reaches a configured, usable state without editing anything the guide does not mention.

checks.title: The product's main flow works
checks.what_to_do: Exercise the one thing the product exists to do, end to end, with real input. The record's deployment guide names the flow for this product.
checks.passing_criteria: The flow produces the expected result on the deployed instance, not only in the product's own documentation.

checks.title: Public exposure and authentication are understood
checks.what_to_do: Establish what the deployment exposes to the internet, what authentication protects it, and what an unauthenticated visitor can reach. Try the product's URL while signed out.
checks.passing_criteria: The exposure is known and intended, and anything reachable without authentication is something the operator meant to be public. 'I did not check' is not a pass.

checks.title: Required persistence survives a restart
checks.what_to_do: Create data the product is supposed to keep, restart or redeploy the service, and look for it again.
checks.passing_criteria: Data that should persist is still there after the restart. For a product that genuinely stores nothing, answer not_applicable and say why.

checks.title: A backup can be taken and restored
checks.what_to_do: Take a backup by the route the product or provider documents, then restore it into a working instance.
checks.passing_criteria: The restored instance carries the data the backup was taken from.

checks.title: An upgrade to a newer version works
checks.what_to_do: Move the deployment from the verified version to a newer released version, applying whatever migration the upstream project documents.
checks.passing_criteria: The upgrade completes and the main flow still works afterwards. Note what broke even when it ends well.

checks.title: Running cost has been observed
checks.what_to_do: Leave the deployment running long enough for the provider to bill or meter it, and read the actual usage.
checks.passing_criteria: A real observed cost or usage figure exists, with the period it covers. An estimate from a pricing page is not an observation.

checks.title: An automated smoke check passes
checks.what_to_do: Run whatever automated check this repository maintains for the product against the deployed instance.
checks.passing_criteria: The check passes. It is evidence about a deployment and never a substitute for a person's verification of the checks above.
